stem:
Tara looks at the diagram of parallelogram $ABCD$. She measures $\angle DAB = 68^{\circ}$ and $\angle ABC = 112^{\circ}$ and notices the opposite angles match in this drawing. She wonders whether opposite angles of every parallelogram are equal.

Which claim correctly decides what her measurements justify?

options.text: The matching angles in this one drawing prove the property for every parallelogram.
Equal opposite angles are what create the parallelogram sides in the diagram.
The measurements support the pattern in this parallelogram; a general property still needs geometric reasoning from known facts.
Any four-sided shape on the page has equal opposite angles once two angles are measured.

teacher.key_rationale: One measured parallelogram shows a useful pattern for that figure; a property for every parallelogram needs geometric deduction. Treating the sample as a full proof, reversing cause, or widening to every four-sided shape leave the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as parallelogram ABCD with measured angles 68° and 112° at A and B.
